scope: Translation-verifier responsibility allocation: two model profiles, three isolated model roles, and host-owned execution and release gates. This record does not activate routing, grant permissions, or change production verification contracts.
evidenceLimits: The small C# to Java low-effort samples completed faster, but case sets and verification effectiveness were not controlled.
The FileUpload high-effort request ended with a connection failure before business tests executed; it provides neither a successful latency baseline nor a model defect-detection score.
Agent session time includes network, orchestration, tools and output generation; it is not a measurement of reasoning time alone.
No specific model profile or latency target in this proposal has been qualified for production.

strong-reasoning.effortPolicy: Use a qualified strong model for independent verification design and unresolved semantic interpretation. Allocate higher reasoning effort to complex state, failure, security or data-integrity obligations; do not assume provider effort labels have identical behavior.
selectionCriteria: Correct requirement-grounded oracles, including source-only and common-mode defects
Evidence-grounded interpretation without weakening approved obligations
Completion rate, latency and cost on permitted enterprise providers and held-out tasks

experimentalCandidate.qualification: Experimental starting point only. Existing low-effort measurements do not establish FileUpload effectiveness or production reliability; the client setting alone is not provider acknowledgment.

fast-code.effortPolicy: Start with low effort for bounded test implementation using frozen obligations, known build commands and existing drivers. Skip model calls when approved tests and adapters already suffice.
selectionCriteria: First-attempt executable tests using real project APIs
Faithful implementation of frozen assertions and required observations
Few harness repair attempts without modifying production code or validation policy
Independently replay-confirmed defect detection, completion rate, latency and cost

stages.runWhen: Every request, before expensive model or build work.
inputs: Approved candidate and request
Language route and required validation policy
Permissions and total request budget
outputs: Capability and toolchain availability
Validated scope and permission boundaries
Deadline or explicit unavailable-capability result
allowedActions: Check actual runtimes, dependencies and supported commands
Fail closed when required capabilities are unavailable
forbiddenActions: Silently fall back to mocks
Ask a model to invent missing capabilities
Treat missing infrastructure as a target behavioral defect

stages.runWhen: After candidate selection; before translation-dependent verification.
inputs: Source implementation bundle
Original target context
Requirements, approved decisions and trusted existing tests
outputs: Versioned and hashed evidence snapshots
Build facts, legal public API invocation and existing test inventory
allowedActions: Collect facts using existing project and language tooling
Use optional bounded fast-model assistance to locate relevant context, then verify cited facts
forbiddenActions: Treat translator conclusions as independent proof
Stage benchmark labels or hidden oracles in model workspaces
Modify user source files

stages.runWhen: Approved reusable obligations do not cover the current requirements and scope; otherwise reuse the unchanged approved artifact.
inputs: Frozen requirements and human decisions
Source evidence and original target APIs
Trusted existing tests and verified engineering facts
outputs: Proposed obligations with IDs, provenance, required flags, inputs, observations and oracle rules
Coverage mapping to existing tests
Ambiguities requiring human confirmation
allowedActions: Design independent requirements-based assertions
Identify allowed differences already supported by the contract
Request clarification for unsupported assumptions
forbiddenActions: Infer correctness solely from source or generated target outputs
Use final translation code to weaken core obligations
Approve its own ambiguous requirement interpretations

stages.runWhen: Before new test implementation or reuse; unresolved requirement ambiguities block the affected obligations.
inputs: Proposed or reusable verification obligations
Required human approvals and fixed validation policy
outputs: Frozen, versioned obligations and approved comparison rules
Executable checks or explicit gaps requiring test implementation
allowedActions: Validate structure, references, policy coverage and required approvals
Bind obligation identity to requirements and evidence snapshots
forbiddenActions: Treat structural schema validity as proof that an oracle is semantically correct
Automatically approve model-proposed requirement waivers

stages.runWhen: Existing trusted tests and approved drivers do not cover frozen obligations. Source drivers and target API adapters may be prepared alongside translation.
inputs: Frozen obligations and trusted tests
Approved driver templates and writable test paths
Verified construction, invocation, dependency and build facts
outputs: Source and target test drivers
Obligation-to-test and observation mapping
Test file hashes and unresolved implementation gaps
allowedActions: Write new tests only within host-authorized isolated paths
Repair test syntax, imports and invocation mistakes without weakening assertions
forbiddenActions: Modify production implementations, existing acceptance tests or build verification policy
Change expected values to match observed failures
Skip required cases or swallow exceptions to obtain pass
Use reflection to bypass required public API access

stages.runWhen: The translator supplies a final patch, and again for each approved repair patch.
inputs: Frozen original target context
Authorized patch and patch hash
outputs: Isolated patched target workspace
Final API and dependency facts or detected incompatibilities
allowedActions: Apply the patch within approved boundaries
Check final implementation against frozen API and dependency constraints
forbiddenActions: Modify the real user workspace during verification
Reuse target execution evidence for a different patch hash

stages.runWhen: Required tests or approved reusable equivalents are ready. Source-only build and execution may be prepared earlier when all source-side inputs are fixed.
inputs: Frozen obligations and mapped tests
Isolated source and final target workspaces
Host-approved commands, budgets and input generators
outputs: Build and test outcomes
Case-linked raw outputs, command IDs and artifact hashes
Returned values, output bytes, state transitions, resource and exception observations
Timeouts and infrastructure failures
allowedActions: Run existing tests and bounded property or generated-input exploration
Capture evidence and minimize counterexamples
Validate generated test mappings and observation completeness
Terminate process trees at deadlines
forbiddenActions: Trust model-authored execution claims without actual records
Run untrusted generated tests outside isolation
Treat zero process exit status as proof that every required assertion ran

stages.runWhen: Execution finishes or terminates; preserve partial and missing evidence explicitly.
inputs: Case-linked execution evidence
Frozen independent assertions and approved comparison rules
outputs: Per-obligation pass, fail or unverified results
Source, target and common-mode defect evidence
Unresolved semantic differences with minimal supporting context
allowedActions: Recompute assertions and compare approved observable behavior
Distinguish target defects from source defects and infrastructure failures
forbiddenActions: Accept model-written mechanical verdicts without recomputation
Equate source-target equality with requirement correctness
Classify missing required observations as pass

stages.runWhen: A material difference remains unresolved by approved rules. Skip this call when mechanical evidence is decisive.
inputs: Frozen contract and approved differences
Minimal counterexamples and raw evidence references
Only the source and target context needed to explain unresolved behavior
outputs: Evidence-grounded interpretation proposal
Supplemental test requests or human clarification requests
Explicit unresolved obligations
allowedActions: Explain differences in a fresh session separate from translator and test-builder sessions
Recommend bounded supplemental observations with a preserved audit trail
forbiddenActions: Override a failed required assertion
Approve a new semantic waiver
Modify tests, production code, policy or raw evidence
Issue the final release decision

stages.runWhen: All relevant stage outcomes are known, including skipped optional model calls; failures also produce explicit incomplete results.
inputs: All required obligation outcomes
Raw execution evidence and integrity checks
Semantic proposals and any independently approved resolutions
outputs: Verification report and persisted receipt
Patch-bound gate result and remaining risks
Timing, model usage, artifact references and cleanup outcome
allowedActions: Assemble reports directly from captured artifacts
Preserve failed and unverified obligations
Persist the receipt and apply cleanup policy
forbiddenActions: Let a model author authoritative command records or final gate status
Release while a required check failed or remains unverified
Treat explanatory prose as substitute execution evidence

parallelPreparation: After explicit candidate selection, prepare frozen obligations, source builds and reusable drivers alongside translation.
Target execution must use the final applied patch; invalidate preparation when its source, requirement, dependency or API assumptions change.
Run source and target commands concurrently only in independently isolated directories without baseline-scan races.
reuse: Prefer existing trusted tests and versioned driver templates; sufficient reusable coverage permits zero model calls.
Bind reusable artifacts to relevant source, dependency, toolchain, runtime, environment, input, requirement, policy and driver hashes; target results additionally require the final patch hash.
Reject unsupported reuse for uncontrolled time, randomness, network or mutable external state; preserve tenant and repository permission boundaries.
escalation: Use strong reasoning for complex verification obligations; reserve semantic review for differences unresolved by approved rules.
If bounded fast-code attempts cannot implement a frozen test correctly, stop automatic fast-code retries and explicitly escalate that task to a strong model or human without expanding permissions.
Missing dependencies, denied commands and connection failures require infrastructure diagnosis or bounded host retry, not more speculative model reasoning.
Supplemental tests return through implementation, execution and mechanical evaluation; they cannot remove or weaken frozen obligations.
budget: The host owns the request deadline, model-call and test-repair limits, exploration limits, cancellation and cleanup reserve. Concrete values remain pending measurement, not promised latency targets.
All retry and supplemental-evidence paths share the total request budget; stage dependencies describe the nominal acyclic flow rather than an unrestricted agent loop.
Reuse valid completed artifacts after a retry only when their identities and integrity match; deadline exhaustion preserves unverified obligations.
Measure complete user waiting time separately from verifier request time and parallel preparation cost; never add nested command time twice.
gate: Host-owned required checks cannot be removed or downgraded by any model. A failed required check blocks release; any required unverified check also blocks release.
A confirmed target failure may coexist with incomplete checks; retain both, rather than masking the incomplete checks with an overall failure label.
Allowed differences must already follow approved rules or receive explicit human approval and a versioned contract update before reevaluation.
Schema validation confirms document structure only. Runtime permission enforcement, obligation coverage, test integrity, evidence linkage and semantic correctness require separate controls.
independence: Use three isolated logical roles with two model profiles; do not create one permanent agent per stage or language side.
Core obligation design must not depend on final translation outputs or translator self-assessment. Source behavior is evidence, not an absolute oracle.
Using a different model does not by itself establish independence; protect approval, test, implementation and evidence boundaries.
Keep benchmark labels, control patches and hidden oracles outside model workspaces; evaluate generated tests through independent mutant-control replay.

repairBoundary.modelSelection: Outside the verifier's two profiles. Select according to defect complexity and the registered translation route; no new translator model is selected by this document.
triggers: Host-confirmed required target failures with actionable compile or behavioral evidence
constraints: The production verifier remains verify-only and never repairs the target implementation.
Preserve the existing finite repair limit and current required-unverified stop behavior in adaptation-adapter-v2; changing that behavior requires a separate reviewed contract change.
The translator cannot modify required checks, independent oracles, evidence, approval rules or test policy.
revalidation: Bind every repair attempt to a new patch hash and preserve the triggering failure evidence.
Reuse unchanged source evidence only with matching cache identity; rerun required target checks for the new patch, including affected regressions and newly added inputs.

metrics: First-attempt executable tests, assertion fidelity and harness repair count
Independently replay-confirmed defect detection, false release and false alarm rates
Unverified rate, report validity and request completion rate
Request p50/p95 with sample counts, first-defect latency, preparation cost and queue time when measured
Model calls, tool calls, token usage and per-stage duration with explicit unknown time
comparisonRules: Qualify models on fixed independently checked obligations and seeded faults; retain held-out tasks not used for tuning.
Change one experimental factor at a time: model, requested effort, prompt, host orchestration or agent harness.
Keep infrastructure failures visible in all-request statistics and separately report semantically evaluable samples.
Do not interpret the initial three materialized variants as full coverage of the designed dataset; extended scenarios require materialization and independent oracle confirmation first.
